newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian rights activist sees no end to violence.
newsitem.headline: Algerian rights activist sees no end to violence.

text.p: Algerian human rights activist Abdennour Ali Yahia told the French daily Le Monde in an interview published on Monday that violence in his country's civil strife is worse than reported and the end is not in sight,
The left-of-centre opponent of the Algerian government is president of the independent Algiers-based League for the Defence of Human Rights (LADDH).
He said the flare-up which has killed more than 100 people in two weeks was to be expected during the Ramadam Moslem fast.
But he also said the government had provoked Moslem fundamentalist rebels by declaring that they had been crushed.
"Every time the government claims security successes there is a violent reaction on the other side," he said.
Newspapers said a car bomb killed 23 people in central Algiers on Sunday and dozens of villagers were massacred in Medea province, a stronghold of the Armed Islamic Group (GIA).
"Killings in many villages go unreported because the press is controlled," Yahia said.

"I believe that the five-year-old policy of all-out security to which the government devoted all its efforts and huge funds is a failure which has actually spread violence to the entire country," Yahia said.
"There is no serious indication that (violence) will decrease in the near or distant future," he said.
About 60,000 people have been killed in civil violence in Algeria since the cancellation in 1992 of a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
Yahia said both the Algerian army and the rebels, competing to win over the people to their side, had unleashed a deadly escalation of killings and revenge.
"This is what fuels the civil war...It is an endless cycle," he said. "The side that wins over the people will win the war."
But he added that there would be no military solution and only dialogue could solve the crisis.
